definitions.gloss: adherence; fixation; being hung up on
definitions.explanation: Stubbornly clinging to something, being overly attached to details, rules, or preconceptions. Almost always carries a negative nuance.

examples.japanese: {形式|けいしき}に{拘泥|こうでい}する{必要|ひつよう}はない。
examples.english: There's no need to be hung up on formalities.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}に{拘泥|こうでい}していては{前|まえ}に{進|すす}めない。
examples.english: You can't move forward if you cling to the past.

examples.japanese: {細|こま}かいルールに{拘泥|こうでい}するあまり、{本来|ほんらい}の{目的|もくてき}を{見失|みうしな}ってしまった。
examples.english: By fixating too much on minor rules, they lost sight of the original purpose.

notes: A formal, literary word. Almost always used with に: 〜に{拘泥|こうでい}する (to be fixated on...). Carries a negative nuance — the attachment is seen as excessive or unhelpful. Common objects: {形式|けいしき}に{拘泥|こうでい}する (fixate on form), {過去|かこ}に{拘泥|こうでい}する (cling to the past), {細部|さいぶ}に{拘泥|こうでい}する (be hung up on details). Compare with the more colloquial こだわる, which can be either positive or negative.
